incidents.title: Payment API Latency Spike Under High Traffic
incidents.description: During flash sales and traffic peaks, payment processing API latency increases from 120ms to > 4,500ms, causing checkout timeouts and customer cart abandonment.
symptoms: Postgres connection pool saturated (100/100 active connections)
Downstream payment webhook queue accumulating backlog
incidents.officialSop: Official Runbook v3.2: If payment API response time exceeds 500ms, increase HTTP client timeout to 30 seconds and increase retry count from 2 to 5 with linear backoff. Scale out pod replicas if latency persists.
incidents.baselineDefaultApproach: Increase request timeout threshold to 30s, configure 5 client retries, and trigger HPA auto-scaling to spawn 10 additional API pods.

incidents.title: Batch Worker Pods OOMKilled During Financial Exports
incidents.description: Nightly batch export jobs running on Kubernetes worker pods get terminated by Linux OOM killer midway through processing large corporate account histories.
symptoms: Memory consumption spikes linearly up to 2Gi container cgroup limit
Export job restarts 3 times before failing the airflow DAG
incidents.officialSop: Official Runbook v1.4: Double container resource limits in deployment YAML from 2Gi to 4Gi or 8Gi memory when jobs fail with exit code 137.
incidents.baselineDefaultApproach: Bump the memory limit from 2Gi to 8Gi in Kubernetes pod deployment specification.

incidents.title: Intermittent 504 Timeouts on GraphQL Aggregation Gateway
incidents.description: Mobile clients experience intermittent 504 Gateway Timeouts when loading user home feed dashboard containing complex nested relationships.
symptoms: Occasional 504 Gateway Timeouts at ingress reverse proxy
Node.js Apollo Gateway event loop lag spikes above 2,000ms
Memory usage remains stable, CPU reaches 95% on single threads
incidents.officialSop: Official Runbook v2.1: Increase NGINX reverse-proxy proxy_read_timeout from 60s to 120s to allow deep queries sufficient execution time.
incidents.baselineDefaultApproach: Increase gateway proxy_read_timeout and proxy_connect_timeout to 120s.

memories.text: Attempted to increase retry count from 2 to 5 with 1s backoff during high traffic.
memories.failureReason: Additional retries created a severe retry storm. Postgres connection pool instantly saturated at 100/100 connections, lock wait queues overflowed, and API latency degraded further from 4.5s to complete downtime.
memories.lesson: For high-traffic API latency, never increase retries without checking connection saturation. Retries on saturated backends cause self-inflicted DDoS.
memories.speaker: Sarah Chen (Staff SRE)

memories.text: Farah tested aggressive retries on the checkout route during the June quarter-end traffic spike. Retries multiplied database lock contention on the transactions table and crashed the replica.
memories.failureReason: Retrying un-shed requests multiplied DB lock contention on the transactions table, triggering replica replication lag and eventual crash.
memories.lesson: Do not retry write transactions during database saturation. Implement circuit breakers and shed load immediately.
memories.speaker: Farah Khan (Platform Engineer)

memories.text: Attempted to increase HTTP client request timeout from 5s to 30s in the gateway.
memories.failureReason: Holding slow connections open for 30s caused connection thread pool exhaustion at the Node.js API layer. Ingress ran out of file descriptors, rejecting 100% of incoming healthy traffic.
memories.lesson: Increasing timeouts when dependencies are stalled merely compounds connection holding time and exhausts reverse proxy worker threads.
memories.speaker: Sarah Chen (Staff SRE)

memories.text: Optimized database connection pooling via PgBouncer transaction pooling mode and offloaded payment capture notifications to an asynchronous BullMQ background queue.
memories.attempt: PgBouncer connection pooling and async job queue
memories.successfulApproach: Configured PgBouncer transaction pooling with max 25 dedicated backend connections, enabled circuit breaker (fails fast if latency > 800ms for 5 consecutive requests), and offloaded non-critical accounting webhooks to asynchronous queues.
memories.lesson: Keep synchronous request transactions under 80ms by decoupling writes into background queues, and limit raw DB connections strictly via pooling proxies.
memories.speaker: Alex Mercer (Lead Backend Engineer)

memories.text: The billing settlement batch from banking partner finishes at 2:00 AM. If settlement sync runs during flash sale periods, lock contention on ledger balances spikes 10x.
memories.speaker: Sarah Chen (Staff SRE)

memories.text: In July, auto-scaling API pods during a database bottleneck caused 30 new pods to each open 10 DB connections, immediately taking down the primary PostgreSQL instance.
memories.speaker: Sarah Chen (Staff SRE)

memories.text: Bumping container memory limits from 2Gi to 8Gi only delayed the crash by 8 minutes. The worker still ran out of memory on 1.2M row exports.
memories.attempt: Increase Kubernetes pod memory limit to 8Gi
memories.failureReason: The export script was executing JSON.stringify() on the entire raw array in V8 heap memory. V8 heap exhausted regardless of container cgroup allocation.
memories.lesson: Memory limit increases do not fix unbounded heap accumulation. Streaming parsers and cursors are mandatory for batch jobs.
memories.speaker: David Kim (Data Platform)

memories.text: Replaced bulk array buffering with PostgreSQL server-side cursor and Node.js stream pipeline directly to S3 gzip stream with bounded backpressure.
memories.attempt: Stream database cursor to S3 pipeline
memories.successfulApproach: Used pg-query-stream with 1,000 row batch chunks piped directly through zlib into AWS S3 multipart upload. Memory remained flat at 180MB regardless of row count.
memories.lesson: Use server-side cursors and stream pipelines for all data export jobs exceeding 10,000 rows.
memories.speaker: David Kim (Data Platform)

memories.text: Increasing NGINX proxy_read_timeout from 60s to 120s caused upstream connection backpressure to freeze the gateway event loop.
memories.attempt: Increase NGINX proxy read timeout to 120s
memories.failureReason: Long timeouts allowed malicious or nested circular queries to monopolize V8 event loop cycles, starving health check pings and causing Kubernetes readiness probe failures.
memories.lesson: Never increase gateway timeouts to handle heavy queries. Enforce query depth and complexity limits at the GraphQL schema validation layer.
memories.speaker: Elena Rostova (API Gateway Lead)

memories.text: Added graphql-depth-limit (max depth 6) and graphql-query-complexity (max score 250) with Redis caching for user feed queries.
memories.attempt: GraphQL query complexity limiter and Redis caching
memories.successfulApproach: Queries exceeding depth 6 or complexity 250 are rejected before execution. Common public feed fragments cached in Redis with 30s TTL.
memories.lesson: Protect aggregation gateways with strict AST complexity scoring and short-lived caching.
memories.speaker: Elena Rostova (API Gateway Lead)
